subject: Acceptance criteria and tradeoffs: latency vs throughput for multi-region StellarHealth pilot
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Lee <anna@stellarhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Acceptance criteria and tradeoffs: latency vs throughput for multi-region StellarHealth pilot

Hi Anna —

Thanks again for the demo earlier — good discussion. As promised, I wanted to capture the open items we need to qualify the pilot from a performance/SLO and geo-routing perspective so our solutions and pilot config map to your expectations. Please confirm or correct any items below so we can ship a concrete pilot proposal.

High-level asks (please confirm with engineering/stakeholders):
- Target latency SLOs (p50/p95) for:
  - typical short prompts (2–20 tokens output)
  - longer completions / batched requests
  - streaming responses (per-token latency expectations)
- Expected concurrency and throughput:
  - steady-state concurrent requests
  - typical QPS and peak burst QPS (and duration of bursts)
- Regional/residency constraints:
  - Are EU patient requests required to remain in EU? Any APAC residency needs?
  - Log/metric retention and whether logs may leave region (audit requirement)
- Security/compliance must-haves: SOC2, encryption-at-rest keys (KMS/HSM), support for customer-managed keys

To keep things actionable, if you can reply with concrete numbers (e.g., p50 < 60 ms, p95 < 250 ms for short prompts; steady concurrency 200; peak 800 for <= 5 minutes) we'll use that to size dedicated pools, propose routing policy (region affinity vs strict locality), and pick an initial batch/quantize profile.

Attachments: I'm attaching a first-cut pilot_sla_matrix_v1.pdf that maps common tradeoffs (batching vs latency; quantization vs quality; dedicated vs shared).

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) You confirm the numbers above (or we capture in a short reply).
2) We propose two pilot configs (latency-optimized and cost-balanced) and a perf-test window.
3) Run a 48–72 hour perf test in staging with synthetic traffic that mirrors your mix.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick 30-min call with engineering if that helps finalize numbers.

—
Markus Klein
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Anna Lee <anna@stellarhealth.com>

Cc: StellarHealth Sales Ops <salesops@stellarhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2026 10:12:43 -0400
Subject: Re: Acceptance criteria and tradeoffs: latency vs throughput for multi-region StellarHealth pilot

Markus —

Thanks for the clear note. I ran this by our platform team; below are the numbers and constraints we can commit to for the pilot. Caveat: these are acceptance criteria for the pilot only — final SLA numbers may tighten after production rollouts.

SLO targets (pilot):
- Short prompts (user-facing autocomplete / short suggestions): p50 < 70 ms, p95 < 300 ms
- Typical completions (200–500 tokens): p50 < 200 ms, p95 < 700 ms
- Streaming: per-token p50 < 100 ms, p95 < 350 ms (we're tolerant of slightly higher p95 during bursts)

Concurrency / throughput:
- Steady-state concurrency: 180 concurrent requests
- Typical QPS: 90 QPS (multi-tenant mix across our app)
- Peak bursts: up to 750 QPS for up to 10 minutes (happens during nightly batch updates)

Geo / data residency:
- US & EU residency required. EU patient data must remain in EU region for storage and inference. US patient data must remain in US. APAC: not required for pilot but may be needed later.
- Logs/metrics: 30-day retention. We cannot allow raw request content to be exported outside the assigned region. Aggregated telemetry is fine to centralize.

Security/compliance:
- SOC2 Type II required before production.
- We will need support for customer-managed keys (KMS) and audit logs for key operations.

Attachments: I've uploaded a short perf-mix sample to your shared Drive folder (perf_test_windows.csv) and can share synthetic traces.

If the above looks doable, let's schedule the perf-testing window the week of Aug 2 — our engineers will be available most mornings EST. Also, please send the proposed pilot configs (latency-optimized + cost-balanced).

Best,
Anna
Anna Lee | Director of Engineering, StellarHealth
anna@stellarhealth.com | +1 (617) 555-0134

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Anna Lee <anna@stellarhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2026 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acceptance criteria and tradeoffs: latency vs throughput for multi-region StellarHealth pilot

Karthik / Evelyn —

Anna sent the numbers (see below). High-level notes and tradeoffs we should communicate back quickly:

1) Feasibility summary (quick):
- Short prompts p95 < 300 ms and streaming p95 < 350 ms are achievable with region-affine dedicated pools, tight batching, and prefix caching.
- Peak bursts to 750 QPS will need either (a) reserved headroom via Dedicated pools sized for bursts or (b) autoscale + cross-region burst fallback. Straight shared-hosted capacity likely won't be predictable enough for the 10-minute burst profile.

2) Suggested pilot config (attachments: proposed_pilot_config.json):
- Dedicated pools: one EU pool, one US pool (G4-equivalent), pinned to the model variant with quantization profile Q4_1 for cost-balanced and a non-quantized variant for latency-optimized.
- Routing policy: region-affinity (US->US, EU->EU) with a relaxed fallback rule to spill to US for EU only in the event of sustained capacity loss (we'll need SLA language).
- Caching: enable prefix/KV cache for common prompts to shave p50 by ~20–30 ms.
- Batching: conservative batching window (8–12 ms) for cost-balanced; zero/near-zero batching for latency-optimized tests.

3) Test & instrumentation asks:
- We need the perf_test_windows.csv + a few representative traces (Anna said she uploaded sample).
- We'll supply a lightweight harness that can replay the mix and measure token-level latency, cold-starts, and KV cache hit rates.
- Proposed perf-testing window: Aug 3–5 (setup Aug 2). Markus to confirm calendar.

4) Compliance notes:
- For EU-residency hard requirement: we'll ensure inference and logs retention for EU are configured to stay in-region; aggregated telemetry will be tagged and ingested centrally with redaction controls.
- KMS: we can support customer-managed keys; need to scope key provisioning and rotation policy in follow-up doc.

Action items (short):
- Karthik: draft the two pilot configs and perf-run playbook (include exact instance types and sizing).
- Evelyn: coordinate with Anna on access, test accounts, and API keys; confirm perf-test engineers availability Aug 3–5 mornings EST.
- Markus: push perf harness & initial SLA matrix to the shared Drive.

I'll attach the proposed_pilot_config.json and a small CSV with suggested test windows.

—
Markus

Attachment: proposed_pilot_config.json, perf_test_windows.csv

Thanks — quick summary and next steps from my side:

Summary:
- Pilot will run with two configs: latency-optimized (pin to non-quantized model, minimal batching, dedicated pools) and cost-balanced (Q4_1 quantization, small batching windows).
- Routing: strict region-affinity with documented fallback policy (spill only under sustained capacity loss >60s).
- Expected test dates: Aug 3–5 (setup Aug 2) mornings EST.

Deliverables I will share by EOD Fri:
1) Pilot sizing doc (instance types, GPU counts, expected steady vs burst headroom).
2) Perf runbook with exact API calls, synthetic mix, and measurement points (token-level latency, p50/p95, error rates).
3) Draft SLO language we can put in the pilot agreement (p50/p95 targets + test pass criteria).

Anna — can you confirm the morning window (EST) on Aug 3–5 for your engineers? Also: please confirm a contact for KMS/key provisioning so we can list required IAM steps in the runbook.
